t: A Native American republic that wrote down its laws from 1808 and adopted a constitution with three branches in 1827.
Sequoyah’s syllabary spread literacy in Cherokee, and the Cherokee Phoenix of 1828 printed English and Cherokee side by side.
Forced west on the Trail of Tears in 1838–1839, the Nation rebuilt at Tahlequah but lost its self-government when Oklahoma became a state in 1907.
dyk: The Cherokee Stand Watie was the last Confederate general in the field to surrender, on 23 June 1865, more than two months after Lee’s surrender at Appomattox.
ev: The Chickamauga Cherokee make peace with the United States at Tellico Blockhouse
The first written Cherokee law creates the Lighthorse Guard
The Cherokee Nation adopts a written constitution
The Cherokee Phoenix appears at New Echota; John Ross is elected principal chief
Worcester v. Georgia rules that Georgia’s laws have no force in the Cherokee Nation
Forced removal on the Trail of Tears begins
An Act of Union reunites the Cherokee, with Tahlequah as capital
Oklahoma statehood ends the Nation’s self-government

f.capital: New Echota (1825–1832); Red Clay, Tennessee (council ground, 1832–1838); Tahlequah (from 1839)
f.predecessor: Cherokee towns of the southern Appalachians, including the Chickamauga Cherokee
f.successor: State of Oklahoma (1907); the Cherokee Nation was later reorganised (constitution of 1975–1976)
